newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Twenty Indonesians arrested after Java riot-paper.
newsitem.headline: Twenty Indonesians arrested after Java riot-paper.

text.p: Indonesian police have arrested more people on charges of looting and destroying property after Thursday's riot in a West Java town, bringing the total number detained to 20, Suara Pembaruan newspaper reported on Saturday.
Police and military officers were not available for comment.

The evening paper quoted chief of the Karawang regency police, Lieutenant-Colonel Harry Montolalu, as saying on Saturday police were still questioning the suspects, but he declined to give further details.
Montolalu was quoted by the Jakarta Post as saying on Friday among the suspects was an ethnic Chinese woman believed to have started the disturbance.

Rioters burned a church and a Chinese Buddhist temple, wrecked four other churches and destroyed and looted shops and homes in the town, which is part of the Karawang regency, a rice-growing area east of Jakarta. Sixteen cars were also destroyed.

Government officials said the riot apparently started after the Chinese woman complained of the noise Moslem youths were making as they beat drums before dawn to summon people to eat before the start of the daylight Ramadan fast.
Residents said on Saturday troops were still stationed in many parts of Rengasdengklok, 50 km (30 miles) east of Jakarta, but people's daily activity had returned to normal.

In Pontianak, capital of west Kalimantan province on the Indonesian side of Borneo island, residents said on Saturday soldiers guarded a number churches after rumours of a possible tribal riot between the native Dayak and people from Madura island, off the main island of Java.

Thousands of people fled Sanggau Ledo, near Pontianak, early last month after a riot sparked by a brawl between the Dayak and the Madurese over a woman. Pontianak residents said some people were afraid to leave home because of the rumours.
Indonesia's armed forces chief General Feisal Tanjung was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying on Friday the military would take sterner measures against rioters.

Last month, four people died when a mob went on a rampage in the town of Tasikmalaya in West Java, setting fire to shops, buildings and churches. That riot was sparked by reports of police brutality towards a Moslem religious teacher.
